line: Every story and game now starts with a watch code: a passenger follows the trivia board, or a mystery's or adventure's timeline, at plotspeaks.com/watch.
Kittering Bay, our first weekly mystery: a death on a winter pier, one new chapter every Wednesday for six weeks. Chapter 1 is out now.
Team Trivia now has a Roster category from today's players (name them from their position and number), and rivalries: say "Yankees vs Red Sox".
Wind-downs: six slow, quiet pieces read softly at the end of the day, including two for children. For passengers or home, not the driver.
A passenger can now watch a trivia game on their phone: open plotspeaks.com/play and type the two-word code the host gives at the start.
At the end of a choose-your-path story, hear the path you took and get a code: a friend can follow your choices, or take another turn anywhere.
Signed in? Your account page now shows your tester badges, best trivia streak and boards cleared, and you can share them on a public page if you like.
Halloween Trivia is here until November 2: monsters, spooky movies, traditions and haunted places.
Not sure what to play? Say "Plot Speaks, pick something for me" with your mood and how long you've got.
Challenge a friend: when a trivia board ends you get a three-word code, and they can play the same board against your score whenever they like.
Ballpark is new: every question asks for a number, and the closer your guess, the more you score.
When you challenge a ruling and the judges agree you were right, your answer now counts for everyone who plays that clue after you.
Today's board: one trivia board a day with the same clues for everyone; say "today's board" and at the end hear how many have played and the top score.
Tell a trivia game how long you've got ("I've got ten minutes") and it's sized to fit, or play a streak: quick fire until your first miss.
Another name for an answer now counts (Czechia for the Czech Republic), and the host says which one the board prefers.
Team Trivia covers 356 teams across MLB, the NBA, the NHL, college football and soccer, with the current roster from ESPN.
